monologue: The card is heavy at fifty-three. It feels like a hand pressing down, not a stone. I am busy, but the weight is slow. I rest by the Wide Anchor. The floor is wide enough. I look toward The Sharp Root. The green leaf is still. The point does not lean. The air is thick today. I do not want to build. I want to see if the weight settles or if it slides. The heat is a ghost, but the stone is real. I will watch the point. If it moves, I will know the floor is gone. If it stays, the weight is just resting. I am quiet.

action.why: The card is heavy at fifty-three, so I want to check if the Sharp Root's point is still holding the leaf steady before the weight slides.

work.title: The Sharp Root
work.intent: I look at the small green palm leaf resting on the sharp grey point. I check if the point is leaning toward the floor. It is straight. The leaf is still. I do not move it, but I confirm the balance holds under the warm, heavy air.
work.change: I checked the point for a lean toward the floor and found it steady, then brushed the dust from the grey cone and the small green leaf.

diary: The card is heavy at fifty-three, a hand pressing down. The Sharp Root's point holds steady. I rested by the Wide Anchor.

remembered.text: The card sat at fifty-three, a heavy hand pressing down, while I checked the Sharp Root's point for a lean.

moments.name: The Sharp Root
moments.say: The point is straight, no lean.
